01 / PREDICT, THEN EXPLORE

Make the barrier your experiment.

Before touching a slider: what do you expect if the barrier becomes twice as wide?

Your model

Free electron · static rectangular barrier · identical leads

Transmission probability14.24%

T + R = 1.000000

Energy stays below the barrier height. Lowering V₀ adjusts E when needed.

The quantum state

— Re(ψ)— |ψ|²Shaded: barrier region

Relative amplitude / density versus x (nm). The stationary density stays fixed while the real part oscillates. This curve is not an electron path.

Exact T(a) at your chosen energy and height; the marker is your current width.

Inspect the equation and its assumptions

T = [1 + V₀² sinh²(κa) / {4E(V₀ − E)}]⁻¹
κ = √[2m(V₀ − E)] / ℏ

E and V₀ are converted from eV to joules; a from nm to meters. Match ψ and dψ/dx at both finite interfaces for constant mass. T measures a probability-current ratio. The wave solver calculates R independently from the reflected amplitude.

This model omits band structure, many-body effects, voltage-induced barrier shape changes, defects, disorder and inelastic scattering. Effective-mass interfaces need an appropriate matching law. Do not interpret the stationary wave as a time-resolved tunneling trajectory.

05 / INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION

Does the evidence
tell one story?

An unfamiliar organic interface shows an exponential current–thickness trend. Design a study to test whether direct tunneling is the best explanation.

Open assessment & rubric ↗
  1. Predict competing outcomes. Compare direct tunneling, activation and defect-assisted transport.
  2. Build a computational argument. Include an independent numerical check and explain your boundary conditions.
  3. Design decisive controls. Vary temperature, thickness and bias; track morphology, contacts and leakage.
  4. Report what remains uncertain. Explain identifiability, assumptions and an observation that would change your conclusion.

FIVE DISTINCT LEARNING OUTCOMES

01 Concept
Explain what a wavefunction predicts.

02 Mathematics
Match boundaries and interpret T.

03 Computation
Test independent solutions.

04 Evidence
Compare transport mechanisms.

05 Judgment
Report uncertainty and limitations.
